cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# demo-coding-agent

A coding agent small enough to understand.

The control loop is sw-MLPL. Rust supplies only filesystem and process
mechanisms that the language cannot express itself. A local LLM supplies
inference through the shipped `llm_call` builtin. The question this repository
answers is not "can MLPL call a model?" but "can MLPL itself express the
control plane of an autonomous software agent?" The target is roughly one LLM
primitive, five OS tools, and one to two hundred lines of MLPL.

[OpenCode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) is the architectural
comparison point. Its conceptual core is a loop:

```text
task -> context -> model -> tool request? -> execute -> observation -> model
```

Everything else in a product-grade agent is engineering layered around that
loop. This repository builds the loop in the open and postpones the layers.

## How it is built

- **Policy in MLPL.** Prompt construction, action parsing, tool dispatch,
  permissions, retry, and stop logic are MLPL data and pure functions.
- **Mechanisms first from builtins.** sw-MLPL already ships sandboxed
  `read_text`, `write_text`, `fs_walk`, and friends, confined to the project
  root. The first agents use no Rust at all.
- **Mechanisms then from a narrow Rust extension.** Allow-listed process
  execution, git diff and status, and search live in `extensions/agent-tools`,
  built on the ABI and SDK pattern proven in
  [`demo-extensions`](../demo-extensions). The model is never handed a shell.
- **Language changes last.** An sw-MLPL request needs an executable probe
  recorded in the [capability ledger](docs/sw-mlpl-capabilities.md).
- **Tests need no model.** Every agent takes its model as an injected
  function reference; mlplunit suites replay scripted transcripts. Live
  Ollama runs are opt-in demos.

The model speaks a tiny text protocol instead of native tool-calling JSON so
the mechanism stays visible:

```text
READ <path>
SEARCH <text>
WRITE <path> ... END
RUN <command>
DONE <summary>
```

## Planned progression

| version | shape                               |
|---------|-------------------------------------|
| v0      | READ, THINK                         |
| v1      | READ, SEARCH, THINK                 |
| v2      | READ, SEARCH, EDIT, TEST            |
| v3      | repeat until tests pass             |
| v4      | planner, builder, reviewer          |
| v5      | budgets, compaction, loop detection |

See [progression](docs/progression.md) for what is deliberately postponed.

## Prerequisites

- The adjacent `../sw-mlpl` checkout with `target/release/mlpl-repl` or an
  absolute `MLPL` override (0.22.0 or newer for `llm_call` and the sandboxed
  filesystem builtins).
- `mlplunit` on `PATH`, an absolute `MLPLUNIT` override, or the adjacent
  `../../softwarewrighter/mlplunit` checkout.
- [`just`](https://github.com/casey/just) for repository task aliases.
- For live runs only: an Ollama or llama.cpp server and a coding model such
  as `qwen2.5-coder`, selected by explicit environment variables.
- Rust 1.85 or newer and `sw-checklist`, only once `extensions/agent-tools`
  exists.

The scripts select existing tools; they never install or overwrite them.

## Development process

Work is divided into durable Agentrail steps. In each fresh session run
`agentrail next`, then `agentrail begin`; implement only that step; run the
precommit gate; commit source and `.agentrail/` metadata; then run
`agentrail complete`. [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) holds the full protocol.

The precommit gate is:

```sh
just check
```

Today it checks repository structure, peer license parity, documentation
links, the generated Agentrail briefing, and canonical MLPL style. Each step
that adds executable behavior extends it with mlplunit suites and, for Rust
crates, `sw-checklist` and scoped `cargo test`.

Read the [architecture](docs/architecture.md), [delivery plan](docs/plan.md),
[saga queue](docs/sagas.md), [permissions](docs/permissions.md), and
[capability ledger](docs/sw-mlpl-capabilities.md) before implementing an
agent. The original design discussion is retained in
[`docs/research.txt`](docs/research.txt).

## Current status

Foundation only. No agent runs yet. The next step measures the builtins an
agent depends on and adds mlplunit infrastructure.

Copyright (c) 2026 Michael A Wright. Distributed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

cat > AGENTS.md <<'EOF'
# Agent Instructions

This repository uses Agentrail sagas and `AGENTS.md` as its single instruction
source. Do not create a duplicate `CLAUDE.md`.

## Repository policy

- Work directly on `main`; do not create feature branches or pull requests.
  This project rule overrides the generic branch-handoff guidance above.
- Follow `agentrail next`, `agentrail begin`, work, test, commit,
  `agentrail complete`, then stop. Never hand-edit Agentrail-managed state.
- Commit source, documentation, tests, and durable `.agentrail/` state together
  before completing a step. Stage named files, never broad worktree sweeps.
- Treat every sibling repository as read-only. Record separately actionable
  work in `docs/cross-repo-handoffs.md`; never change a sibling from here.
- Never install or overwrite stable user tools. Prefer explicit absolute tool
  overrides, then `PATH`, then documented adjacent development checkouts.

## Coding agent contract

- MLPL owns policy: prompts, context, action parsing, tool dispatch,
  permissions, retry, budgets, and stop logic. Rust owns mechanisms only.
- Prefer existing sw-MLPL builtins. Add a function to this repository's Rust
  `agent-tools` extension only for behavior MLPL cannot express (process
  execution, git, and search if the pure-MLPL version measures too slow).
  Request an sw-MLPL change only after an executable probe recorded in
  `docs/sw-mlpl-capabilities.md` proves neither path works.
- Report sw-MLPL bugs and justified improvement suggestions as you meet them.
  Record each in the findings queue of `docs/sw-mlpl-capabilities.md` with a
  minimal probe, expected versus observed behavior, and the affected agent.
  Do not work around a bug silently.
- No primitive ever executes a model-generated string as a shell command.
  Process execution matches a fixed argv allow-list. All file effects stay
  under the `--source-dir` project root.
- Every agent takes its model as an injected function reference. mlplunit
  suites use scripted fake transcripts; live Ollama runs are opt-in demos and
  never the only acceptance evidence.
- Keep each agent version a separate readable file under `agents/`. Favor
  records and pure functions over hidden state.

## Testing and completion gate

- Use test-driven development for executable behavior. MLPL behavior requires
  native mlplunit tests with root `mlplunit.conf`, `tests/test_*.mlpl`, `@test`
  registration, shared assertions, and one `u:run_registered_tests()` call.
  Rust behavior under `extensions/` requires a focused failing test first,
  scoped `cargo test`, and a passing `sw-checklist` on that crate.
- Every tracked `.mlpl` file starts with a module-purpose comment; every
  user-defined function has a first-expression docstring; canonical formatting
  is mandatory.
- Use the root `justfile` as the entry point and keep recipes thin. Portable
  work belongs in `scripts/`; do not add Makefiles.
- Before every commit and push, run `just check`. The gate must include
  structure, documentation links, the generated briefing, MLPL style, and,
  once they exist, mlplunit suites, extension checks, and demos.
- Update README, architecture, permissions, progression, capability ledger,
  handoffs, and saga queue in the same step as affected behavior.
- Inspect `.gitignore` and `git status --short`, stage named paths, commit on
  `main`, push with `git push origin main`, and verify success before reporting
  completion. Never force-push or bypass hooks.
- Run `agentrail complete` only after the implementation commit and successful
  gate. If completion changes durable metadata, commit and push those exact
  files separately, then make no further source changes.
- At the end of every Agentrail step, summarize what was completed, checks run,
  commit/push status, what the next step will deliver, and explicit blockers or
  limitations (`none` when there are none).

Planning references: `docs/research.txt`, `docs/architecture.md`,
`docs/plan.md`, `docs/sagas.md`, `docs/permissions.md`,
`docs/progression.md`, `docs/cross-repo-handoffs.md`, and
`docs/sw-mlpl-capabilities.md`.
EOF

**How to apply:** When planning a step, check the sw-mlpl lang-reference for a builtin before writing Rust. When Rust is needed, put it under extensions/agent-tools using the public ABI/SDK path. Never silently work around an sw-MLPL bug; log it in the ledger with a minimal probe. Related: [[sw-ml-study-repo-conventions]].

The foundation is done and committed. Two commits sit on `main`, unpushed, ready for `git push origin main` when you want them public.

**What I found first.** Two facts in sw-mlpl 0.22.0 reshaped the plan compared with the research transcript. The `llm_call` builtin exists with the optional system argument. More importantly, sandboxed `read_text`, `write_text`, `write_atomic`, `fs_walk`, `file_metadata`, and `run_script` already ship, all confined to the `--source-dir` root. So Saga 1 needs no Rust at all, and the extension is reserved for what MLPL cannot do well: allow-listed process execution, git diff/status, and ripgrep-backed search per your note.

**What I created**, matching demo-ml-microscope and demo-extensions conventions:

- `AGENTS.md` with the generated Agentrail briefing plus project rules. The rules encode your three mid-turn points: builtins before Rust before sw-mlpl requests, ripgrep-crate search in the extension, and recording sw-MLPL bugs and justified improvement suggestions in the ledger rather than working around them.
- `COPYRIGHT` and `LICENSE` byte-identical to peers, `.gitignore`, and a filled-in `README.md`.
- `docs/plan.md` with five sagas, plus `sagas.md`, `architecture.md`, `permissions.md`, `progression.md`, `sw-mlpl-capabilities.md` (the ledger with a findings queue), and `cross-repo-handoffs.md`. `docs/research.txt` is committed.
- A documentation-only `just check` gate: structure and peer license parity, local doc links, briefing freshness, MLPL style. It passes. `sw-checklist` reports no Rust crates yet, as expected.
- Saga `agent-loop-foundation` with five steps. Step 001 (foundation) is begun and completed against the first commit, with a separate metadata commit. `agentrail next` now points at 002.

The Saga 1 steps are: measured builtin probes with mlplunit and the tiny-rust-project fixture, the v0 read/think agent with an injected model so tests never need Ollama, the action protocol parser, and the bounded read/write loop with allow/ask/deny policy as data.

**Two questions**, neither blocking the next step:

1. For the Saga 2 Rust extension, the demo-extensions SDK crates are unpublished at version 0.0.0. I defaulted the handoff doc to a git dependency at a pinned commit rather than a path dependency on the adjacent checkout. Tell me if you prefer the path dependency.
2. Live model runs are wired to require explicit `OLLAMA_HOST` and `OLLAMA_MODEL` and are excluded from `just check`. If you would rather have a default host and model baked into the `just` recipes, say so and step 003 will do that.

content.text:
Bake in `qwen2.5-coder:7b`. You already have it installed on this Mac, and it fits the RTX 3060 12G comfortably.

**Why that model.** The Q4_K_M default pull is 4.7 GB on disk and roughly 6 GB resident with an 8K context, leaving headroom on 12 GB for the KV cache of a prompt that carries file contents and history. It follows a strict "reply with exactly one action" system prompt well, which is what the text protocol needs. The 1.5B and 3B coder variants run anywhere but drift out of the protocol often enough to make the demo about parsing failures instead of the loop. The 14B variant needs about 9 GB at Q4 and gets tight on the 3060 once context grows, so it is a good upgrade tier but a bad floor.

**What to require of contributors.** Require only an Ollama-compatible server and the ability to pull one model. Concretely:

- Recipes default `OLLAMA_HOST` to `http://localhost:11434` and `OLLAMA_MODEL` to `qwen2.5-coder:7b`, both overridable.
- The live-run script checks the tags endpoint first and prints a one-line pull command if the model is absent, instead of failing inside `llm_call`.
- The README states the floor as a 12 GB GPU or a 16 GB unified-memory Mac, and names `qwen2.5-coder:1.5b` as the "it runs anywhere, expect protocol drift" fallback for smaller machines.
- `just check` stays model-free, so forks without a GPU still get a green gate. Only `just v0` and `just loop` touch the server.

Keep the transcript fixtures pinned to `qwen2.5-coder:7b` so recorded live runs are reproducible across your machines. Anyone with a bigger card can set the env var to a 14B or 32B model without touching the repo.

Say the word and I'll fold this into step 003's prompt and the README prerequisites, or you can leave it for the next session to pick up from this conversation.

content.content:
Insert a new pending step at a chosen position, shifting later steps up

Use when a bug or unplanned task needs to slot in before existing pending work. The new step lands at position `after + 1`; every pending/in-progress step with a number greater than `after` shifts up by one (step.toml `number` and the on-disk `NNN-slug` directory name are both updated). The operation is refused if any step that would shift is already `Completed`, since completed steps anchor git-tracked history.

Pass `--after 0` to prepend at position 1 (only works if step 1 is pending).

Cursor semantic (preemption): if the new step lands at or before the current cursor, focus follows the new arrival — the inserted step becomes `current_step` and the previously focused step is pushed to `current_step + 1`. This matches the "drop in a blocker" use case. If the new step lands behind the cursor, focus is unchanged and the new step is queued as future work.

Usage: agentrail insert [OPTIONS] --after <AFTER> --slug <SLUG> --prompt <PROMPT>

Options:
      --after <AFTER>
          Position to insert after (0 prepends). The new step becomes N+1

      --slug <SLUG>
          Slug for the new step

      --prompt <PROMPT>
          Step prompt: text, file path, or "-" for stdin

---
Reopen a completed or blocked step

Transitions the step back to InProgress, clears `completed_at`, and moves the saga cursor to it. The `commits` array is preserved, so any git-history linkage from the original completion stays intact — new work after reopen should be committed on top.

Usage: agentrail reopen <NUMBER>

Arguments:
  <NUMBER>
          Step number to reopen

Options:
  -h, --help

content.content:
# MLPL Emacs Support

## Overview

MLPL includes a full Emacs integration in `elisp/`, providing editing, REPL interaction, SVG visualization, and interactive menus -- all using only built-in Emacs libraries (zero external package dependencies).

## File Structure

```
elisp/
  mlpl-all.el      One-shot loader: loads everything, in order (START HERE)
  mlpl.el          Entry point / loader for the four core modules
  mlpl-mode.el     Major mode for .mlpl files
  mlpl-repl.el     Comint-based REPL integration
  mlpl-svg.el      SVG display (inline + gallery)
  mlpl-menu.el     Interactive SVG menus (tutorial, demos, help)
  mlpl-fold.el     Result folding for long output
  ob-mlpl.el       Org-babel backend (#+begin_src mlpl)
  mlpl-org.el      Org helpers (C-c C-c, table import)
  mlpl-bootstrap.el  All-in-one self-contained bundle (alternative)
```

### Module Dependency Graph

```
=== mlpl-org.el head ===
;;; mlpl-org.el --- Org-mode integration for MLPL -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-

;; Author: MLPL Contributors
;; Keywords: org, MLPL, literate programming
;; Package-Requires: ((emacs "26.1"))

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'mlpl-fold)

(defgroup mlpl-org nil
  "MLPL org-mode integration."
  :group 'mlpl)

(defun mlpl-org-execute-src-block ()
  "Execute the MLPL source block at point."
  (interactive)
  (unless (org-in-src-block-p 'mlpl)
    (error "Not inside an MLPL source block"))
  (org-babel-execute-src-block))

| `run_script(path, opts)` | 1-2 | Execute a script file in a FRESH environment -- definitions, `@test` metadata, and bindings cannot leak between files; `include` and file-accurate spans behave exactly as in normal script runs. Options: `{source_dir, data_dir, capture: 1}` (paths sandbox-resolved). Returns `ok({status, value, value_raw, error, events_kind, events})`: `status` is `"ok"`, `"err"` (the script's final value was an Err), `"error"` (hard eval error), or `"exit"` with the code in `value` -- the child's `exit(n)` is INTERCEPTED as data instead of terminating the process. `value` is a lossy display RENDERING (a string result comes back quoted and cannot be recovered from it); `value_raw` is the child's actual final value UNMODIFIED -- use it to get a real string / record / number back. `capture: 1` buffers the child's typed test events into `events` (one JSON line each). Only un

=== mlplunit README 60-75 ===
runner passes `source_root` from configuration, an explicit `--source-dir`, or
the test file's directory to sw-MLPL as its source sandbox. Repeatable host
`--include FILE` options remain as a compatibility bridge: they prepend sources
between the assertion library and each test in command-line order.

Each test also runs with `--data-dir` rooted at that test file's directory, so
its own MLPL code can use `load("fixture.txt")`. Override the root with
`--data-dir DIR`. In particular, `load("subject.mlpl")` can read MLPL source
as a string, but the language currently has no `eval(string)` operation, so
reading does not import or execute that source.

**Checks run before commit:** `just check` passed in full: structure, doc links, briefing freshness, MLPL style on six files, and 21 of 21 mlplunit probes. `just llm-probe` ran live against the local Ollama and got "PONG" from qwen2.5-coder:7b.

**What was pushed** (commit 921d022, then metadata 6b244e9):

- mlplunit infrastructure: `mlplunit.conf`, `scripts/run-tests`, `just tests`, wired into `just check`.
- Three probe suites under `tests/` pinning the sandboxed filesystem builtins, the `run_script` outcome record, and the string helpers a prefix protocol needs. Fixtures include two committed symlinks, one resolving inside the repo and one to `/etc/hosts`.

- F1: `"a" + "b"` fails with "expected an array value, got a string". The research transcript's pseudo-code relies on string `+`. Agents will use `str_concat` and `str_join`.

"""## Run the v0 agent

```sh
just v0
```

v0 is the whole loop with one tool and no iteration: read one file with
`read_text`, build a `TASK:` / `SOURCE:` prompt, ask the model once, print
the answer. It lives in [`agents/v0_read_think.mlpl`](agents/v0_read_think.mlpl)
as five small functions and [`agents/run_v0.mlpl`](agents/run_v0.mlpl) as the
live entry. The system prompt is the plain file
[`prompts/think.md`](prompts/think.md). `V0_FILE` and `V0_TASK` override the
file and the task.

The model is a function reference. `call(:u:ask_live, host, model, system)`
binds the server details into a one-argument partial; tests bind
`u:ask_scripted` to a fixed reply or pass `u:ask_echo` to inspect the exact
prompt. Against `qwen2.5-coder:7b` the fixture crate yields an explanation of
`add` and a suggested negative-number test.

```sh
just tests        # 26 native mlplunit tests, no model server needed
just llm-probe    # opt-in: one llm_call round trip against local Ollama
```
""")

closure) that the agent invokes with `call(ask, prompt)`; tests bind

### F6. `include` resolves differently under mlpl-repl and mlplunit (tooling)

Probe: `mlpl-repl -f agents/run_v0.mlpl` resolves `include "v0_read_think.mlpl"`
relative to the including file and refuses `../` that leaves `--source-dir`.
mlplunit copies each test to a temporary file, so a file-relative
`include "../agents/x.mlpl"` fails with "no such source file" and the test
must write `include "agents/x.mlpl"` relative to `source_root`. Both are
defensible; the asymmetry means an agent file cannot be included the same
way from a test and from a runner. Suggested improvement: have mlplunit run
tests in place, or document source-root-relative includes as the contract.""")

**What was pushed** (commit 51e8e87, then metadata 6f9f2f4):

- The v0 agent in `agents/v0_read_think.mlpl`: five small functions. It reads one file, composes a task/source prompt, and calls an injected model. A missing file propagates as a Result err without ever asking the model.

**Blockers:** none.

Named function followed by parenthesized, comma-separated arguments.

## Loop Construct

```
repeat N { body }
```

Execute the body N times. N must evaluate to a non-negative integer.
The body can contain multiple statements separated by semicolons or
newlines. Returns the result of the last expression in the final
iteration (or scalar 0 if N is 0).

```
x = 0
repeat 10 { x = x + 1 }
# x is now 10
```

## Training Loop

```
train N { body }
```

Like `repeat`, but additionally binds the iteration index to `step`
inside the body and captures each iteration's final expression value
into a `last_losses` 1-D array in the environment. Use with
`momentum_sgd` / `adam` for training loops:

```
- the `break value` if the loop exited via `break value`
- scalar `0` if the loop exited via bare `break`
- scalar `0` if the loop exited because `cond` went falsy

`continue` skips the rest of the current iteration; the condition
is re-checked. `break` and `continue` are only valid inside a
`while` body -- using either outside raises a runtime error.

```mlpl
# Count up to 5 (loop value is 0; i ends at 5).
i = 0
while i - 5 { i = i + 1 }

content.text:
Step 004 is complete, committed, and pushed. `main` is at f1f8ce5 on origin, tree clean, and Agentrail points at step 005, the last in this saga.

**Checks run before commit:** `just check` passed in full with 41 of 41 mlplunit tests, including the 15 new protocol tests that were written before the parser.

**What was pushed** (commit b061761, then metadata f1f8ce5):

- `agents/protocol.mlpl`: one model reply becomes a tool record or an err. READ, SEARCH, WRITE with an END terminator, RUN split into argv with repeated spaces collapsed, and DONE with a multi-line summary. Verbs must be whole words, so "READING the file" is an unknown verb rather than a read of "ING the file". CRLF is normalized, trailing whitespace and blank lines are ignored.
- Rejections name their reason: empty reply, unknown verb, missing END, more than one action, trailing prose after an action, empty path or argument, a `..` path component, and an absolute path. Dots inside a filename like `lib..rs.bak` are still allowed.
- Architecture doc now describes the parser's exact record shapes. README and saga queue updated.

**Two new sw-MLPL findings in the ledger:**

- F7: choosing among five verbs takes five nested if/else levels because there is no `else if`, `match`, or early return. The record-plus-Result encoding itself reads well. Suggested in order of value: `else if` chaining first, then a string or tag `match` form. A full tagged-sum type is not needed for this demo.
- F8: `a && b` is a lexer error, and there is no `str_trim`, `str_starts_with`, or string-list filter or append. The parser hand-writes trim helpers and collapses repeated spaces by rejoining through a string.

**Next step, 005-v2-bounded-loop:** `agents/loop.mlpl`, the observe, decide, act, update loop over one state record, with allow/ask/deny authorization as a pure function, read and write dispatch over the sandboxed builtins, a "not available yet" observation for search and run, and stops on done, deny, or exhausted budget as values. A scripted multi-turn model proves it; `just loop` runs it live. It closes Saga 1.

**Blockers:** none.

the task and the step limit. The system prompt is

by counting prior actions in the prompt, so every stop reason, the ask

     2	
     3	The demo target is an MLPL project, for fun and because it needs no Rust:
     4	`run_script` already executes an MLPL test file in a fresh environment and
     5	returns its outcome as data, so "edit, run the tests, repeat" is reachable
     6	with builtins alone.
     7

     9	   mlplunit-style test file) and harden the protocol from live transcripts:
    10	   tolerate a ``` fence line directly after `WRITE <path>` and directly
    11	   before `END`, and record each new model habit as a test before handling
    12	   it. Keep the strict rejections.
    13	2. Implement `RUN` for MLPL projects in pure MLPL: an allow-list of the
    14	   form `RUN mlpl tests/test_add.mlpl` that maps to `run_script` with the
    15	   project root as `source_dir`, returning `status`, `value`, and captured
    16	   test events as the observation. Anything else stays "not available".
    17	3. Close the loop on the MLPL target: the agent adds `u:mul` and its test to
    18	   the example project, runs the tests, and finishes when they pass. Prove
    19	   it with a scripted transcript and record a live transcript fixture.
    20	4. Record the VHS demo (see item 8) of that MLPL run for the README.
    21	5. Add `extensions/agent-tools` as a Rust `cdylib` on the demo-extensions ABI
    22	   and SDK, proven by `sw-checklist`, scoped `cargo test`, and a stock-CLI
    23	   `load_extension` check. First functions: `_agent_tools:search(pattern)`
    24	   over the project root, built on the ripgrep crates (`grep-searcher`,
    25	   `grep-regex`, `ignore`) with an `rg` subprocess as the documented
    26	   fallback, and `_agent_tools:run(argv)` against a fixed allow-list
    27	   (`cargo test`, `cargo check`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo fmt`, `git diff`,
    28	   `git status`). The public `agent_tools` facade is MLPL.
    29	2. Express permissions in MLPL as data: `{read: "allow", search: "allow",
    30	   write: "ask", test: "allow", git: "ask", shell: "deny"}`. Authorization is
    31	   a pure function from action plus policy to allow, ask, or deny, tested
    32	   without a model or a filesystem.
    33	3. Close the loop: `SEARCH` and `RUN cargo test` reach the extension, the agent
    34	   iterates until tests pass or the budget is spent, and the example Rust
    35	   project gains a real unit test through a recorded live run.
    36	4. Add `git_diff`, `git_status`, and an exact old/new `patch` mechanism so the
    37	   model edits regions instead of rewriting whole files.
    38	
    39	5. Record the demo. Once the agent actually codes, add `demos/loop.tape`
    40	   for [VHS](https://github.com/charmbracelet/vhs) that runs `just loop`
    41	   on the example task and exports GIF and WebP (and MP4 for the README
    42	   link). The live entry already prints each action and observation as it
    43	   happens so the recording shows the loop, not a final dump. Keep the tape
    44	   deterministic where possible: fixed task, fixed budget, `LOOP_APPROVE=1`,
    45	   and the pinned model.
    46	
    47	Exit: the agent completes "add a unit test and make it pass" against the
    48	example project with every OS effect passing through a permission decision,
    49	and a recorded VHS demo of that run is linked from the README.
    50	
    51	## Saga 3: planner, builder, reviewer

import pathlib, re
p = pathlib.Path("docs/plan.md"); s = p.read_text()
start = s.index("## Saga 2:"); end = s.index("## Saga 3:")
new = """## Saga 2: the agent codes in MLPL, then mechanisms for Rust

The demo target is an MLPL project, for fun and because it needs no Rust:
`run_script` already executes an MLPL test file in a fresh environment and
returns its outcome as data, so "edit, run the tests, repeat" is reachable
with builtins alone.

1. Add `examples/tiny-mlpl-project` (a `lib.mlpl` with one `u:add` and a
   mlplunit-style test file) and harden the protocol from live transcripts:
   tolerate a ``` fence line directly after `WRITE <path>` and directly
   before `END`, and record each new model habit as a test before handling
   it. Keep the strict rejections.
2. Implement `RUN` for MLPL projects in pure MLPL: an allow-list of the
   form `RUN mlpl tests/test_add.mlpl` that maps to `run_script` with the
   project root as `source_dir`, returning `status`, `value`, and captured
   test events as the observation. Anything else stays "not available".
3. Close the loop on the MLPL target: the agent adds `u:mul` and its test to
   the example project, runs the tests, and finishes when they pass. Prove
   it with a scripted transcript and record a live transcript fixture.
4. Record the VHS demo of that MLPL run. Add `demos/loop.tape` for
   [VHS](https://github.com/charmbracelet/vhs) that runs `just loop` on the
   example task and exports GIF and WebP (and MP4 for the README link). The
   live entry already prints each action and observation as it happens so
   the recording shows the loop, not a final dump. Keep the tape
   deterministic where possible: fixed task, fixed budget, `LOOP_APPROVE=1`,
   and the pinned model.
5. Add `extensions/agent-tools` as a Rust `cdylib` on the demo-extensions ABI
   and SDK, proven by `sw-checklist`, scoped `cargo test`, and a stock-CLI
   `load_extension` check. First functions: `_agent_tools:search(pattern)`
   over the project root, built on the ripgrep crates (`grep-searcher`,
   `grep-regex`, `ignore`) with an `rg` subprocess as the documented
   fallback, and `_agent_tools:run(argv)` against a fixed allow-list
   (`cargo test`, `cargo check`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo fmt`, `git diff`,
   `git status`). The public `agent_tools` facade is MLPL.
6. Extend the permission record with `git` and `shell: "deny"`; the
   allow/ask/deny function from Saga 1 stays the single authorization point.
7. Close the loop on the Rust target: `SEARCH` and `RUN cargo test` reach the
   extension and `examples/tiny-rust-project` gains a real unit test through
   a recorded live run. Add `git_diff`, `git_status`, and an exact old/new
   `patch` mechanism so the model edits regions instead of rewriting files.

Exit: the agent completes "add a function and its test and make it pass"
against the MLPL example with no Rust, then against the Rust example through
the extension, every OS effect passing through a permission decision, and a
recorded VHS demo of the MLPL run is linked from the README.

"""
p.write_text(s[:start] + new + s[end:])
q = pathlib.Path("docs/sagas.md"); t = q.read_text()
old = """## Next: mechanisms and permissions

Add the Rust `agent-tools` extension for search, allow-listed process
execution, git diff/status, and exact patching; express allow/ask/deny
permissions as MLPL data; close the loop on "add a unit test and make it
pass"."""
assert old in t
q.write_text(t.replace(old, """## Next: the agent codes in MLPL, then mechanisms for Rust

First target an MLPL example project: `RUN` maps to `run_script` in pure
MLPL, the protocol is hardened from live transcripts (fences, END-less
bodies), and the agent adds a function plus its test and iterates until the
tests pass, recorded as a VHS demo. Then add the Rust `agent-tools`
extension for ripgrep search, allow-listed `cargo`/`git`, and exact patching
to reach the same result on the Rust example."""))
print("plan repaired")
EOF
agentrail plan --update docs/plan.md >/dev/null && cmp docs/plan.md .agentrail/plan.md && ./scripts/check 2>&1 | grep -v "^PASS\|already formatted\|^TEST" | tail -3 && git status --short

git add README.md agents/v0_read_think.mlpl agents/loop.mlpl agents/model.mlpl agents/run_loop.mlpl prompts/act.md scripts/run-loop scripts/check-structure justfile tests/test_loop.mlpl docs/architecture.md docs/permissions.md docs/plan.md docs/progression.md docs/sagas.md .agentrail/plan.md .agentrail/steps/005-v2-bounded-loop/step.toml && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Add the bounded read/write loop with allow, ask, and deny permissions

agents/loop.mlpl is the whole agent as data plus pure functions. One state
record {task, iteration, history, files, budget, done, reason, answer}
flows through build context, ask model, parse action (agents/protocol.mlpl),

Step 005 is complete and Saga 1 is closed. `main` is at 5119347 on origin, tree clean.

**Checks run before commit:** `just check` passed in full with 51 of 51 mlplunit tests. `just loop` ran live twice against qwen2.5-coder:7b: a dry run that stopped at the first write with reason `denied`, and a `LOOP_APPROVE=1` run that read the fixture, wrote the notes file with a proper END, and finished with DONE in three steps.

**What was pushed** (commit c46fc04, then metadata 5119347):

- `agents/loop.mlpl`: the whole agent as one state record flowing through build context, ask, parse, authorize, execute, update. Authorization is a pure lookup of a `{read, search, write, run}` record returning allow, ask, or deny. An ask resolves through an injected decision function, so an unattended run never writes. Stop reasons `done`, `denied`, and `budget` are values. Malformed replies and failed builtins become observations the model sees next turn.
- `agents/model.mlpl` now holds the shared ask functions for both agents. `agents/run_loop.mlpl` prints each action and observation as it happens, which is what a VHS recording needs.
- `prompts/act.md`, tightened after the first live runs showed the model fencing WRITE bodies in markdown and dropping the END line. With the tightened prompt the run completed cleanly.
- Ten loop tests driven by a scripted transcript model that picks its reply by counting prior actions in the prompt.
- The badge is now the verified artwork with transparent blue corners.

**Plan changes from your mid-turn notes:**

- Saga 2 now starts with an MLPL example project. Since `run_script` already runs an MLPL test file and returns its outcome as data, "edit, run tests, repeat" needs no Rust at all. The agent's first real coding task will be adding `u:mul` and its test to that project.
- A VHS tape recording `just loop` on that task, exported to GIF, WebP, and MP4, is Saga 2 item 4. The Rust extension for the Rust example moved to items 5 through 7.
- Protocol hardening from live transcripts, such as tolerating fence lines around a WRITE body, is item 1 with a test per observed model habit.

**Next:** Saga 2 needs a fresh saga. The sequence is `agentrail archive` for the completed one, then `agentrail init` from the plan and `agentrail add` for its steps. Say go and I'll set that up and start step 1, the MLPL example project and protocol hardening.

**Blockers:** none. One caveat: the two badge commits sit outside any step, so `agentrail audit` will list them as unclaimed. That is informational only.

lines: +Build a coding agent small enough to understand. The control loop, prompt
+construction, action parsing, tool dispatch policy, permissions, and stop logic
+are written in sw-MLPL. A local LLM supplies inference through the shipped
+`llm_call` builtin. Filesystem and process mechanisms come first from the
+sandboxed builtins sw-MLPL already ships and then from a narrowly scoped Rust
+`agent-tools` extension that lives in this repository.
+The README proposition is: how little machinery is required to turn an
+array/functional language into a coding agent? The target answer is one LLM
+primitive, roughly five OS tools, and one to two hundred lines of MLPL.
+OpenCode is the architectural comparison point, not the implementation target.
+- `llm_call(url, prompt, model[, system])` is a shipped language builtin
+  (sw-MLPL 0.22.0). It returns the model reply as an ordinary string. There is
+  no streaming, native tool calling, or chat threading, and that is fine: the
+  agent uses a small text action protocol instead.
+- sw-MLPL already ships sandboxed, Result-speaking filesystem builtins:
+  `remove_path`, all confined to the `--source-dir` root with symlinks never
+  followed. Reading, listing, and writing project files need no Rust.
+- `run_script` executes an MLPL file in a fresh environment and returns its
+  outcome as data. It runs MLPL only; it cannot run `cargo test` or `git`.
+- sw-MLPL has no search-in-files, no allow-listed process execution, and no
+  git access. These are the mechanisms a Rust extension must supply. Search
+  is expressible as `fs_walk` plus `read_text` plus `str_find`, but a
+  ripgrep-backed extension respects `.gitignore`, handles binaries, and
+  scales; it is the planned path rather than a fallback.
+- `../demo-extensions` proves the extension path this repository will reuse:
